curation.notes: Polymer mechanochemistry: AFM-SMFS (homemade AFM, toluene, ambient) pulling of synthetic polymers bearing cyclobutene mechanophores, whose force-triggered disrotatory ring-opening appears as a plateau; contour lengths before/after the plateau fitted with an extended FJC model and compared with CoGEF calculations. No biological molecule is involved and no controlled experiment_class fits (covalent mechanochemistry), so experiment_class is left empty.

entities.name: Cyclobutene mechanophore-containing polymers (Me and trimethylsilyl alkyne substituted variants)

evidence.snippet: All pulls that reached forces up to 2 nN exhibited a characteristic plateau region in the force curve, wherein the polymer lengthens as a result of the irreversible ring-opening of cyclobutene mechanophores.
pulling experiments were conducted in toluene under ambient conditions using a homemade AFM.

applies_to.transition: disrotatory ring opening; stabilization per Me substituent on scissile C-C bond

source.snippet: Theory and experiment reveal that the formally forbidden reaction is more sensitive to substituents on the scissile carbon-carbon bond than on the alkene, with each of two Me substituents providing approximately 1.5-2 kcal mol-1 of stabilization

applies_to.transition: disrotatory ring opening; stabilization by trimethylsilyl alkyne substituent

source.snippet: with each of two Me substituents providing approximately 1.5-2 kcal mol-1 of stabilization and a trimethylsilyl alkyne substituent approximately 4.5-6.5 kcal mol-1.
